/-!
# Conjecture 6.60

by V. P. Shunkov

Do there exist infinite finitely generated simple periodic (conjugacy) biprimitively
finite groups which contain both involutions and non-trivial elements of odd order?

Here (following Shunkov) a group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if for every finite
subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two elements of prime order in the quotient $N_G(H)/H$ generate
a finite subgroup. It is *conjugacy biprimitively finite* (now also called a *Shunkov
group*) if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two conjugate elements of prime
order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. Every biprimitively finite group is
conjugacy biprimitively finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

theorem kourovka.«6.60» : answer(sorry) ↔

claims.decomposer_note: Primary reading without the parenthetical: does there exist a group G that is infinite, finitely generated, simple, periodic (torsion), biprimitively finite (Shunkov: for every finite subgroup H, any two elements of prime order in N_G(H)/H generate a finite subgroup), and has an element of order 2 and a non-trivial element of odd order; a yes/no existence question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ G ...), with 'biprimitively finite' needing a local definition since it is not in Mathlib.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state this slot identically in substance: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsSimpleGroup G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ IsBiprimitivelyFinite G ∧ (∃ g, orderOf g = 2) ∧ (∃ g, g ≠ 1 ∧ Odd (orderOf g)), with the bespoke IsBiprimitivelyFinite := ∀ finite subgroup H, ∀ x y in H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer of prime order, Finite (closure {x,y}). I verified the elaboration (Finite ↥H, quotient via Mathlib's Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer instance, Finite ↥(closure {x,y}); orderOf = 0 for infinite order is not prime, so only genuine prime-order elements are constrained; H = ⊥ is included so the condition applies to G itself). c07 chosen as the base for its clean definitions plus the two short proved API lemmas the style guide requests for bespoke definitions; docstrings lightly edited (module docstring borrowed from c03/c04 wording).

claims.decomposer_note: The Kourovka parenthetical asks the same existence question for the larger class of conjugacy biprimitively finite groups (for every finite subgroup H, any two *conjugate* elements of prime order in N_G(H)/H generate a finite subgroup); since biprimitively finite implies conjugacy biprimitively finite, this is a weaker existence claim subordinate to the primary one, all other hypotheses (infinite, finitely generated, simple, periodic, contains involutions and non-trivial odd-order elements) unchanged.
claims.reviewer_why: Same existence statement with IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (adds IsConj x y in the quotient N_G(H)/H as an extra hypothesis, so it is the larger class, matching the notebook's parenthetical). All candidates agree; c04 dropped the redundant (orderOf y).Prime, which is equivalent since conjugate elements have equal order, but I kept the literal form with both prime hypotheses. The implication biprimitively finite ⇒ conjugacy biprimitively finite is recorded as a proved API lemma, confirming the subordination noted in the decomposition table.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's two slots (primary reading without the parenthetical, plus the conjugacy variant) match the statement, and the definitions it gives for (conjugacy) biprimitively finite agree with Shunkov's standard definitions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.60

by V. P. Shunkov

Do there exist infinite finitely generated simple periodic (conjugacy) biprimitively
finite groups which contain both involutions and non-trivial elements of odd order?

Here (following Shunkov) a group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if for every finite
subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two elements of prime order in the quotient $N_G(H)/H$ generate
a finite subgroup. It is *conjugacy biprimitively finite* (now also called a *Shunkov
group*) if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two conjugate elements of prime
order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. Every biprimitively finite group is
conjugacy biprimitively finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.60»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two
elements of prime order in the quotient $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *conjugacy biprimitively finite* (a *Shunkov group*) if for every finite
subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two conjugate elements of prime order in the quotient $N_G(H)/H$
generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → IsConj x y → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- Every finite group is biprimitively finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every biprimitively finite group is conjugacy biprimitively finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.isConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (h : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G) :
    IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy _ => h H hH x y hx hy

/--
Do there exist infinite finitely generated simple periodic biprimitively finite groups
which contain both involutions and non-trivial elements of odd order?

Here a group $G$ is biprimitively finite if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.60» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsSimpleGroup G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      IsBiprimitivelyFinite G ∧
      (∃ g : G, orderOf g = 2) ∧ (∃ g : G, g ≠ 1 ∧ Odd (orderOf g)) := by
  sorry

/--
Do there exist infinite finitely generated simple periodic conjugacy biprimitively finite
groups which contain both involutions and non-trivial elements of odd order?

Here a group $G$ is conjugacy biprimitively finite if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$,
any two conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. This is
the reading of Problem 6.60 with the parenthetical "(conjugacy)" included. Since every
biprimitively finite group is conjugacy biprimitively finite, a positive answer to
`kourovka.«6.60»` gives a positive answer to this question.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.60».variants.conjugacy : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsSimpleGroup G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G ∧
      (∃ g : G, orderOf g = 2) ∧ (∃ g : G, g ≠ 1 ∧ Odd (orderOf g)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.60»

items: 'Any two elements of prime order' in the definition of biprimitively finite is read as each element having prime order, with the two primes not required to coincide (in the conjugacy variant the primes automatically coincide since conjugate elements have the same order).
N_G(H)/H is modeled as H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer, using Mathlib's instance Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer for the quotient group structure.
'Generate a finite subgroup' is modeled as Finite ↥(Subgroup.closure {x, y}).

The finite subgroups H range over all finite subgroups including the trivial subgroup (so in particular any two elements of prime order in G itself generate a finite subgroup), which is the standard reading of Shunkov's definition.

'Involution' is modeled as orderOf g = 2; 'non-trivial element of odd order' as g ≠ 1 ∧ Odd (orderOf g) (orderOf g = 0 for infinite order is even, so it is excluded automatically; periodicity makes this moot anyway).
'Simple' uses Mathlib's IsSimpleGroup, which includes Nontrivial G (implied anyway by Infinite G).
The existential quantifies over G : Type (universe 0), matching the convention of the other Kourovka files in the repository.
In the conjugacy definition both (orderOf x).Prime and (orderOf y).Prime are kept as hypotheses alongside IsConj x y for literal faithfulness, even though one of them is redundant.

Two short proved @[category API] lemmas (finite groups are biprimitively finite; biprimitively finite implies conjugacy biprimitively finite) are included as basic API tests for the bespoke definitions, per the style guideline.

reviewer_notes: Both slots ship. Final file composed from c07 (definitions, theorems, API lemmas) with docstring text adapted from c03/c04; compiles with only the two 'declaration uses sorry' warnings. Independently confirmed all eight candidate files compile cleanly. One ambiguity a human should be aware of: the definition of 'biprimitively finite' used here (and specified in the decomposition notes, and adopted unanimously by all candidates) does not require the two prime-order elements of N_G(H)/H to have the *same* prime order. Some renderings of Shunkov's definition say 'two elements of the same prime order'; under that reading the class is larger and the primary existence claim slightly weaker. For the conjugacy variant the two readings coincide (conjugate elements have equal order), so that slot is unaffected. Other modeling choices: periodic = Monoid.IsTorsion, finitely generated = Group.FG, simple = IsSimpleGroup (includes Nontrivial, implied by Infinite anyway), involution = orderOf g = 2, non-trivial odd-order element = g ≠ 1 ∧ Odd (orderOf g); carrier quantified over Type as in other Kourovka files (a finitely generated group is countable, so no universe loss).
